concept.name: Reduce-only order
concept.definition: An order instruction, standard on derivatives and crypto exchanges, that permits the order to only reduce an existing open position: any portion that would increase or reverse the position is rejected or canceled. It is used to guarantee that stop-loss or take-profit orders cannot accidentally open a new position.
concept.intuition: Reduce-only is a safety latch: 'this order may shrink my position but must never grow it' - so a late-triggering exit order can't flip you long when you meant to be flat.
concept.mechanics: The venue checks the order against the current position before executing; if execution would increase the position (or none exists), the order is rejected or its quantity is clamped/canceled. On Bybit, for example, reduceOnly = true means the position can only reduce in size if the order is triggered, and reduce-only orders submitted with no open position are refused.
concept.failure_modes: If the position was already closed by another order, the reduce-only exit order is canceled, which is intended - but traders relying on it as a stop can be left with a residual position if the reduce-only quantity was clamped below the full size. Venue-specific priority rules may cancel distant reduce-only orders under margin stress.
concept.misconceptions: Reduce-only is not itself an order type like limit or market; it is a modifier on another order. It also does not guarantee an exit at a particular price - only the direction of position change.
concept.example: You are long 2 BTC perpetuals and place a reduce-only sell limit for 2 BTC; if the position is closed manually first, the reduce-only order is canceled instead of opening a 2 BTC short.
